title: The Bible Never Told You to Follow Your Heart… and That Might Be Why You’re Tired
paragraphs: The Bible Never Told You to Follow Your Heart… and That Might Be Why You’re Tired
What if the voice you’ve trusted the most… is the very one leading you further away from peace?
Somewhere along the way, we were taught something that sounds beautiful but is quietly dangerous.
“Follow your heart.”
It sounds freeing. It sounds brave. It feels honest.
But Scripture never said it.
Not once.
In fact, the Bible says something far more unsettling.

In Jeremiah 17:9, the Hebrew reads:
“עָקֹב הַלֵּב מִכֹּל וְאָנֻשׁ הוּא מִי יֵדָעֶנּוּ”
(‘Aqov ha-lev mikol ve’anush hu, mi yedā‘ennu)
“The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately sick; who can understand it?”
Deceitful.

Not misunderstood.
Not wounded.
Deceitful.
That word “עָקֹב” (aqov) carries the idea of being crooked, twisted, even fraudulent.
Your heart doesn’t just feel deeply.
It can lie convincingly.
And suddenly… everything starts making sense.
Why you chased something that felt right but left you empty.
Why you trusted someone your spirit was warning you about.
Why you kept returning to what God already called you out of.
Because it felt right.
Because your heart said yes.
And now you’re exhausted.
Not because you’re weak… but because you’ve been following something unstable.
Even Jesus didn’t trust the human heart.

In John 2:24–25, the Greek says:
“αὐτὸς δὲ Ἰησοῦς οὐκ ἐπίστευεν αὐτὸν αὐτοῖς… ἐγίνωσκεν τί ἦν ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ”
(autos de Iēsous ouk episteuen auton autois… eginōsken ti ēn en tō anthrōpō)
“Jesus did not entrust Himself to them… for He knew what was in man.”
He knew.

The instability.
The contradictions.
The way we can cry out to God one moment… and betray Him the next.
That same heart Peter had when he said, “I will never deny You,” only to break hours later.
That same heart David had when he worshiped deeply… and then fell into scandal.
This is not about shaming you.
This is about waking you up.
Because if you keep following your heart without surrendering it to Christ… it will keep leading you in circles.

Proverbs 3:5 says in Hebrew:
“בְּטַח אֶל־יְהוָה בְּכָל־לִבֶּךָ וְאֶל־בִּינָתְךָ אַל־תִּשָּׁעֵן”
(Betach el-YHWH be’khol-libbekha, ve’el binatkha al tisha’en)
“Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding.”
Did you catch that?
You don’t follow your heart.
You surrender it.
You don’t lean on your understanding.
You lay it down.
Because your heart was never meant to lead you.
It was meant to be led.
And this is where everything changes.
Because God doesn’t just expose the problem… He offers transformation.

Ezekiel 36:26 says:
“וְנָתַתִּי לָכֶם לֵב חָדָשׁ”
(Ve’natatti lakhem lev chadash)
“I will give you a new heart.”
Not improved.
Not repaired.
New.
A heart that no longer deceives you… but aligns with Him.
A heart that doesn’t chase what destroys you… but desires what heals you.
This is the Gospel.
Not behavior modification.
Heart transformation.
And maybe this is why you’ve been feeling that quiet tension lately.
That pull between what you feel… and what God is saying.
That internal conflict you can’t ignore anymore.
That’s not confusion.
That’s conviction.
And conviction is mercy.
Because Jesus doesn’t leave you trapped in your own desires.
He rescues you from them.
This is where scandal turns into grace.
Because every wrong turn your heart made… every decision you regret… every place you wish you never went…
Jesus can rewrite it.
Not erase it.
Rewrite it.
Romans 8:28 reminds us that God works all things together for good for those who love Him.
Even the things your heart led you into.
Even the things you’re ashamed to talk about.
Even the version of you that didn’t listen.
He’s not finished with you.
But you have to stop following your heart… and start following Him.
Be honest.
This hit deeper than you expected, didn’t it?
Let this be the moment you stop trusting your emotions more than God’s Word.
And when it does… come back here.
If you truly want to glorify God, then don’t just agree with truth… support the spread of it.
Because following your heart might feel right… but following Jesus will make you whole.
And one day, you’ll thank God He didn’t let your heart have the final say.
